record.original_question: Let G ⩽ Sym(Ω) be a finite primitive permutation group with a regular suborbit(that is, G has a trivial 2-point stabiliser). Then is it true that for all α, β ∈ Ω, there exists γ ∈ Ω such that the 2-point stabilisers Gα,γ and Gβ,γ are both trivial?

evidence.quote: Let G ⩽ Sym(Ω) be a finite primitive permutation group with a regular suborbit(that is, G has a trivial 2-point stabiliser). Then is it true that for all α, β ∈ Ω, there exists γ ∈ Ω such that the 2-point stabilisers Gα,γ and Gβ,γ are both trivial?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega$ be a finite set and let $G \leq \mathrm{Sym}(\Omega)$ be a primitive permutation group. For $\alpha, \beta \in \Omega$, write $G_{\alpha,\beta} = G_\alpha \cap G_\beta$ for the pointwise stabiliser of the pair $\{\alpha,\beta\}$. The orbits of a point stabiliser $G_\alpha$ on $\Omega$ are called the suborbits of $G$, and a suborbit $\Delta$ is called regular if $G_\alpha$ acts regularly on $\Delta$; equivalently, $G$ has a regular suborbit if and only if there exist $\alpha, \delta \in \Omega$ with $G_{\alpha,\delta} = 1$.

Assume $G$ has a regular suborbit. Decide whether the following statement is true: for every pair $\alpha, \beta \in \Omega$, there exists $\gamma \in \Omega$ such that
$$G_{\alpha,\gamma} = 1 \quad \text{and} \quad G_{\beta,\gamma} = 1.$$
artifact.status_search_result: This is the Burness–Giudici (BG) conjecture concerning the Saxl graph of a finite primitive permutation group of base size 2 (vertices $\Omega$, edges given by pairs with trivial joint stabiliser); the question asks whether every two vertices have a common neighbour. The conjecture is open in general but has been verified in many families, including primitive groups with socle PSL(2,q), PSU(3,q), Sz(q), or Ree(q), and various product-type and diagonal-type cases. No counterexample is known.

status_evidence.title: Burness–Giudici conjecture for rank-1 Lie type groups
status_evidence.snippet: The BG-Conjecture: if G is a finite primitive permutation group with b(G)=2, then every pair of vertices in its Saxl graph has a common neighbor. ... we prove the conjecture for primitive groups with socle Sz(q) or Ree(q).
status_evidence.claim: The problem is the Burness–Giudici conjecture, open in general and recently proved in additional cases.

status_evidence.title: On base sizes for primitive groups of product type
status_evidence.snippet: Saxl graph and the Burness–Giudici common-neighbour conjecture for primitive groups; results for product-type groups.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture has been investigated and partially verified for product-type primitive groups.
